Role resolution uses Service.CallerRole, which lists every member of the organisation on each internal pull. Acceptable behind inference-core's 30 s cache, but add a point query (like IsActiveMember) before enforce is switched on for large organisations.
Policy writes leave only the history table; no audit event is published to the control audit stream. WS06 consumes the history rows, but a published event would be needed for tamper-evident audit.

The rows evaluated by mp-contracts (availability and refusal kinds, plus the permit and route rows) have no Rust evaluator yet; S3 must add tests/model_entitlement_matrix.rs and vendor the golden to mp-contracts/tests/fixtures. The refusal and availability rows are specification only until then.

explain does not return projection_revision or any signal that the member role may lag auth-core, and custom role names beyond owner, admin, member and viewer are only matched by exact lower-cased name.

A default model can be checked at write time only against exact entries; when the allow list holds provider selectors the default is accepted and only inference-core can refuse it later (comment in validate.go). Also the 64 KB body limit is tested at the handler, not against the delegation 1 MB cap interplay.

results.notes:
What is built (org-core, no caller until S3, no switch needed):
- Migration 021 (up and down): org_model_policies, org_model_policy_revisions, append-only org_model_policy_history (runtime role can only select and insert), RLS per table in the 019 template, all cascading from organizations(id), so gdpr_hard_delete_organization removes them without being redefined.
- Package internal/modelentitlement: types, ValidatePut (exact ids or provider:<id>, no globs, 500 entries, 128 chars, 20 roles, 16 surfaces, 64 KB body, max_effort must be one of the six WS11 rungs, min_privacy_tier closed set, default model must pass its own policy, default effort at or below max_effort, every problem reported at once), pure Resolve and Policy.Permits (role override replaces the org default, deny wins, a call with no user gets the org default only), a Repository (compare-and-set on the revision row taken FOR UPDATE, policy rows and history written in one transaction, revision and rows read in one statement), and a Service.
- Routes: GET and PUT /api/v1/organizations/:id/model-entitlement and its /orgs/:id form, GET .../explain[?user_id=], GET /internal/orgs/:orgId/model-entitlement?user_id= (scope org:model-entitlement:read:any, Cache-Control no-store). The PUT guard is the membership guard plus owner or admin from the membership table, never the forwarded role header. Stale revision gives 409 with current_revision. SetModelEntitlements is wired in main.go. The service-auth scope tables are updated.
- run-control-plane.sh mints INFERENCE_ORG_CORE_SERVICE_TOKEN.
- Golden apps/Model Plane/api/contracts/model-entitlement-matrix.json with 32 rows, vendored byte for byte into org-core testdata. The six required rows are present. The Go side evaluates the resolve, permit, route and shape rows. The availability and refusal rows are marked for mp-contracts (S3).
- The status is partial because the docker-compose.yml lines are not mine to apply and the Postgres test could not run here.

Decisions taken (flag any you disagree with):
- A named user who is not an active member gets nothing only when the organisation has a policy. An organisation with no policy stays state none, so a lagging membership projection cannot lock anyone out of an organisation nobody restricted. The plan row says "non-member = nothing" without that qualifier.
- GET of the whole policy set is owner or admin only; the plan names only the scope. Explain for oneself is open to any active member; explain for another user is owner or admin.
- A blank user_id on the internal route is a 400, not a service call, so a caller bug cannot widen a person to the org default.
- history columns are named before_set and after_set, not before and after, to avoid keyword risk.
- config/plane-service-principals.json is unchanged: it is the plane-token registry for auth-core, and the inference-core org-core credential is a service token in the compose registry.
